author: Valérie Ouellet, Michelle Allan
description: Less than a week after an exclusive CBC investigation revealed over 1.5 million Canadian Crime Stoppers tips were compromised in a massive data breach, the fallout continues to grow, with more Crime Stoppers chapters and police services suspending their use of the program.
title: Canada-wide freeze on Crime Stoppers programs, partnerships surges to 35 agencies
Hamilton and Niagara regions head to the polls to choose next municipal governments

description: Former FBI director ‌James Comey is facing a third criminal case from ​U.S. President Donald Trump's administration, ​accusing him of sharing sensitive ​national security information, according to court documents ‌made public on Monday.
title: Trump administration tries to prosecute former FBI director James Comey for 3rd time

author: Sheena Goodyear
description: When Sarnia, Ont., Mayor Mike Bradley first spotted an unusual, unmanned vessel in the St. Clair River, he says he thought it looked "like something from Mars." Then he found out it was one of several surveillance sail drones deployed to the Great Lakes this summer by the U.S. Coast Guard.
title: The U.S. put surveillance drones in the Great Lakes, and this border town mayor isn't happy

author: Marcus Medford-Kerr
description: Debbie Shields took a seat on a New York City subway and ended up joking with comedian Conan O'Brien about their fictional family. Their exchange on internet talk show SubwayTakes went viral. The Brooklyn bar owner says she's always making people laugh, but this experience was surreal.
title: How this Brooklyn bar owner had Conan O’Brien in stitches on SubwayTakes

description: A United Nations commission says Israel ​continued to commit genocide in Gaza after last October's U.S.-brokered ceasefire in the enclave, in a report published Monday that Israel dismissed as part of a "misinformation campaign."
title: UN commission says Israel has continued to commit genocide in Gaza since truce

author: Jessica Wong
description: Rights-holders of Elvis Presley's music catalog have sued Anthropic for more than $41 million US, accusing the artificial intelligence giant of tapping the King of Rock and Roll's songs without consent to train its AI models and 'infringing copyrights at an unfathomable scale.'
title: Elvis Presley's music rights-holders sue Anthropic over songs used for AI training

author: Jaspreet ​Singh
description: Microsoft said on Monday it is offering voluntary buyouts to more than a quarter of its global workforce — including in Canada — as the technology giant looks to contain costs and help fund its ‌massive AI investments.
title: Microsoft gives voluntary buyout offer to about 60,000 employees

description: Prime Minister Mark Carney takes questions from journalists at the First Nations-first ministers meeting in Ottawa, the first such meeting in two decades.
title: Carney holds news conference at meeting with First Nations leaders, premiers

author: Natalie Stechyson
description: The parents of a 3-year-old soccer player in Florida say the police were called to a game this weekend because their son was dominating the ball. Police have confirmed with CBC News they were called to the game over reports of an "unruly parent."
title: Florida parents say police called to 3-year-old's soccer game because kid was 'too good'

author: Nicole Brockbank
description: Self-described "Crypto King" Aiden Pleterski admitted his $300-million fund never existed in a June 2022 audio recording played in court at his fraud trial in Toronto on Monday.
title: 'Crypto King' trial hears recording of Aiden Pleterski admitting $300M fund 'never existed'

description: Officials on opposite sides of the African continent are trying to determine how a woman diagnosed with Ebola in Nigeria's capital last week contracted the deadly virus without having visited the Democratic Republic of Congo — the epicentre of one of the worst human outbreaks of the virus in history.
title: Nigeria Ebola patient flown to Switzerland, Congo health worker killed as 4 countries deal with outbreak

author: Jillian Kestler-D'Amours
description: Canadian lawmakers heard from several experts on Monday morning as a parliamentary committee studies the impact of artificial intelligence on women, girls and 2SLGBTQ+ individuals.
title: Women 'risk being left behind' in AI push, advocates warn Canadian lawmakers

author: Alexandra Mae Jones
description: Singer Chris Brown has avoided immediate imprisonment for attacking a music producer in a London nightclub in 2023, with a U.K. judge handing him an eight-month suspended sentence.
title: Chris Brown gets suspended 8-month sentence for 2023 nightclub attack, avoiding jail

description: Actor Walter Koenig, who played Ensign Pavel Chekov, the youthful Russian navigator on the Star Trek television series and several movies, has died. He was 90.
title: Walter Koenig, Ensign Chekov on Star Trek: The Original Series, dead at 90

author: Peter Zimonjic, Louis Blouin, Katie Simpson
description: With the U.S.-Canada trade war dominating the final days of the U.S. midterm campaign, trade discussions between the two countries have intensified. But sources tell CBC News and Radio-Canada that doesn't mean a deal is imminent.
title: Canada-U.S. trade talks intensifying but wide gap remains, sources say

description: The Trump administration last year illegally fired Maurene Comey, the daughter of former FBI director James Comey, from her job as a federal prosecutor in New York, a federal judge ruled Monday.
title: Judge rules Trump administration illegally fired prosecutor Maurene Comey, daughter of ex-FBI director

author: Verity Stevenson
description: The horse-drawn carriage industry is again getting a lot of neigh-sayers, after New York City council passed a bill last week that would ban the rides by June 2028.
title: Horse-drawn carriages are still a tradition in some Canadian cities

author: Tori Fitzpatrick
description: The companies say Umios plans to establish High Liner Foods as the core platform for its North American business, while maintaining its headquarters in Nova Scotia.
title: High Liner Foods to be bought by Umios in deal valued at $804M

description: Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre has asked Prime Minister Mark Carney to repeal the oil tanker ban on British Columbia's northern coast months after Canada inked a deal not to change it.
title: Federal Conservatives renew push to end B.C. North Coast tanker ban

author: Jonathan Ore
description: Gamers, developers and critics lamented the closure of revered studio BioWare, with many crediting its works for kickstarting their own careers in the games industry.
title: Gamers, developers praise BioWare's envelope-pushing games following 'heartbreaking' closure

description: Artificial intelligence giant Anthropic filed papers on Monday for what could be the biggest initial public offering of stock ever.
title: AI giant Anthropic files papers to sell shares to the public for 1st time

author: Nicholas Frew
description: Elections Alberta officials are finishing counting referendum ballots, but the results so far suggest Albertans in rural areas seem to hold different views on immigration and constitutional fights than those living in urban areas.
title: Alberta referendum tallies reveal rural-urban divide on ‘the 9’

description: Canada has received its first pair of new F-35 fighter jets, with Ottawa still deliberating over how many of the American planes it will buy.
title: Canada receives first F-35 jets from U.S., as full order remains under review

author: Boshko Maric
description: Guy Lapointe Jr., Quebec's new domestic security, said both the police ethics commissioner and the province's independent police watchdog, known as the BEI, will look into the allegations.
title: Montreal police officer faces ethics probe for allegedly urinating on homeless people

description: Eric Bauza of Scarborough, Ont., the Emmy-award winning voice actor best known for the iconic Bugs Bunny, has died.
title: Eric Bauza, modern voice of Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck and others, dead at 46
Toronto’s mayoral campaign is ending in a tight race. Here's how it got so close
Voters cast ballots across GTA with polls set to close at 8 p.m.

description: Jordanian security forces arrested three armed suspects after a shootout on Monday in connection with an attack on a church last week that killed nine people, state television reported.
title: Jordan arrests 3 suspects in deadly church attack, state media says

author: Alicia Wang
description: A Manitoba man living with a rare genetic condition says he's now considering medically assisted dying, after being denied out-of-province coverage to get a procedure he and experts say he can't get here.
title: Manitoban denied out-of-province care for rare condition says he's 'tortured every single day'

description: On Tuesday, Israelis will head to the polls for the first time since October 7th. Could this be the end of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s tenure?
title: Will Israeli voters turf Netanyahu?

author: Kate Dubinski
description: A heartwarming video that shows a Londoner stopping to give warmth to a sleeping homeless couple offers an example of kindness and a stark reminder that institutions need to do better, a local man says.
title: Video of man helping homeless couple should inspire compassion and change, building manager says

author: Ariana Kelland
description: Group homes and residential care placements ensure children without a home have somewhere to live, and ideally, to thrive. A CBC News investigation has found that's not always the case.
title: Reports show staffing shortages, training lapses and care failures in N.L. group homes

author: Inayat Singh
description: After a seven year wait and a circuitous path through the justice system, a climate lawsuit against the federal government is finally getting its trial hearings this week in Vancouver.
title: Historic lawsuit challenging government over climate inaction begins trial hearings

author: Annabelle Olivier
description: The city of Montreal passed a motion asking the Quebec government to create a mandatory rent registry and to cap rent increases to inflation over a three-year average. Housing advocates are praising the move, but not everyone is on board.
title: Montreal wants rent control, mandatory registry. What would that look like?
